entry.title: Week 2 – Building AI Agents with CrewAI and Generative AI Hub
entry.content:
This exercise introduces AI agent development by combining CrewAI (an agent framework) and SAP's Generative AI Hub as the LLM provider to create intelligent, task-oriented agents.

Welcome to week 2 of the April Developer Challenge on AI! Last week you learned how to build a RAG use case with the grounding service and the orchestration service. This week you'll build an AI agent using CrewAI, and Generative AI Hub.

What You'll Achieve

By working through this exercise, you'll learn how to:

  • Build Your First AI Agent: Create an intelligent agent with a specific role, goal, and backstory using the CrewAI framework
  • Define Agent Tasks: Structure concrete objectives and expected outputs that guide agent behavior
  • Integrate Multiple Technologies: Connect CrewAI with LLMs via SAP Generative AI Hub
  • Process Complex Queries: Enable agents to analyze user input, make decisions, and provide structured recommendations

The exercise implements a Hamburg Social Welfare Case Manager agent that can process citizen inquiries, assess eligibility for welfare programs, and generate personalized support plans. This demonstrates how AI agents can be designed to handle domain-specific scenarios requiring structured analysis and decision-making capabilities.

What is CrewAI?

CrewAI is a third-party open-source Python library. As the name suggests, you can use it to build a crew of agents that have a set of tools available to accomplish certain tasks. CrewAI uses tasks to bridge the gap between high-level goals and concrete agent actions, assigning specific objectives and expected outputs. For now, your agent will only respond to incoming queries.

Implementation Components

Agent Configuration

The Hamburg Social Welfare Case Manager agent is configured with:

  • Role: Hamburg Social Welfare Case Manager
  • Goal: Process and manage social welfare applications, matching citizens with appropriate services
  • Backstory: Experienced case manager with deep knowledge of Hamburg's social services
  • LLM: Uses sap/gpt-4o from Generative AI Hub
  • Verbose Mode: Enabled for detailed execution tracking

Task Definition

Tasks in CrewAI define:

  • Description: Specific instructions for processing user inquiries
  • Expected Output: Structured assessments with eligibility determination and support plans
  • Agent Assignment: Links the task to the welfare agent

Interactive Workflow

The system includes:

  • User input prompt for welfare inquiries
  • Dynamic task creation based on user questions
  • Crew execution with verbose output
  • Formatted assessment report generation

Testing Your Agent

Try asking various social welfare questions to test the agent's capabilities in:

  • Analyzing citizen circumstances and needs
  • Determining eligibility for welfare programs
  • Recommending local services and resources
  • Creating personalized support plans

Additional Resources

  • Challenge Blog Post
  • Week 1 Challenge - INCLUDING INFO ON HOW TO GET STARTED!!
  • Example Repo
  • CodeJam on code-based agents

To participate: Submit a screenshot of your last cell including output as a comment below! 

You can find the week 2 exercises in the same repo/workbook from last week in the file week2_agent.ipynb 🙂

entry.title: 🇩🇪 Build Code-Based AI Agents on SAP Business Technology Platform (Berlin, Germany)
entry.content:
In this CodeJam, you will learn how to build state-of-the-art AI agents using the Generative AI Hub and Python. You will also gain the skills to create custom tools for your agents, including leveraging SAP's RPT-1 model. Finally, you will deploy your agents to SAP BTP (cloud foundry) and add them to Joule.In this CodeJam you can choose to build your agents with Python and CrewAI or LangGraph.

The CodeJam will include the following SAP technologies:
Generative AI Hub on SAP AI Core

  • SAP RPT-1
  • Grounding Service
  • SAP AI Launchpad
  • Business Application Studio (Python)

Exercise Content:  https://github.com/SAP-samples/codejam-code-based-agents

Prerequisites: 

  • Bring your own laptop with power adapter and have a supported Chromium-based browser
  • It can be helpful to bring a tablet or second laptop, if you have one, to have the instructions on a separate screen.

Location and Date:

This is a free in-person event and is planned for Tuesday, September 15th, in Berlin from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM local time. The event's language and content will be in English. 

Event Address: Zalando SE - BHW, Hedwig-Wachenheim-Straße 7, 10243 Berlin, Germany

  • A huge thank you to Zalando for hosting this event.
  • The instructor is SAP Developer Advocate @noravonthenen 

Please note that spaces are limited! We can only accommodate 35 attendees. If you want to attend, register by clicking the Yes button in the Will you be attending? section above to the right. Approximately 1 week prior to the event, you will receive an email to confirm your attendance, along with further instructions and details.

entry.title: 🟣 Bring AI into Your ABAP Applications with ISLM: Build, Integrate, and Consume AI Natively
entry.content:
Explore how ISLM provides an ABAP-native foundation to consume SAP-delivered AI scenarios and build custom AI solutions directly within SAP S/4HANA—without additional middleware. See how the ABAP AI SDK, powered by ISLM, enables seamless AI integration into ABAP applications and business processes.
Learn how ISLM supports classical AI and Generative AI, enabling governed integration, consumption, and lifecycle management, while also supporting low-code AI development.
Get a sneak peek at Tabular AI and the latest capabilities, including System-Triggered Agents, laying the foundation for the autonomous enterprise.

Abhishek Mishra, SAP

Priti Dhingra, SAP

entry.title: AI Eating Brains! How I Fed Mine to Joule Work Desktop
entry.content:
Now that the title caught your attention, let's talk about how to increase personal productivity by contextualizing Joule Work Desktop. JWD is powerful: it compliantly reads your email, your calendar, and with the right MCP connector, your personal knowledge base too. In this session I'll show you how to wire your personal notes into JWD and what changes when your AI assistant can finally see what you know. Pre-meeting briefings assembled without opening a file. Semantic search that finds meaning across your notes, not just keywords. Sprint notes updated from a chat message. We'll also look at how JWD extends beyond your note vault and I'll share what I learned building the note connector itself using contract-driven AI coding.

Mathias Kemeter, SAP

entry.title: Unlocking Tabular Foundation Models: From Experimentation to Production
entry.content:
In this session, we walk you through the full developer journey of building a production-ready tabular AI solution. Starting from model validation in the Playground — including explainability and the sandbox API — we move step by step towards productizing your solution using the Tabular AI Orchestration Layer.
You will learn how to register and manage context, run orchestration via REST APIs or dedicated skills, and seamlessly integrate tabular predictions into your applications — including your AI agents.
Whether you are just exploring tabular foundation models or ready to ship, this session gives you the practical know-how to go from first experiment to production.

Katharina Schell, SAP

entry.title: Enable Your AI application to Run on Multiple Models to Ensure Resilience and Compliance
entry.content:
Learn why AI applications should not depend on one model and how you can enable your application to support multiple models using AI Core services and features like, prompt optimization, evaluation and Orchestration fallbacks.

Franziska Dobrigkeit, SAP

entry.title: Combining AI Agents with the power of SAP HANA embedded ML (part 2)
entry.content:
Discover how to enhance AI agents with SAP HANA's embedded machine learning capabilities. In this session, you'll learn to equip code-based AI agents with predictive models built using the SAP HANA Predictive Analysis Library. See how to integrate custom machine learning models as agent tools, empowering your agents to derive insights from your data and make smarter, data-driven decisions. The technology stack of this agent includes SAP BTP, SAP HANA Cloud and the Python SDKs for both SAP HANA and the Generative AI Hub.

Nora von Thenen

Witalij Rudnicki

entry.title: 🟣 How We Make Tabular Predictions in 2026 with TabPFN
entry.content:
Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) allow us to make predictions over tabular data without needing to train a model with domain-specific data. What this means in practice is one model for virtually infinite predictions. In this talk, we'll cover what makes TFMs different, how they learn from your historical data and make predictions in a single-pass, and what that means for AI agents in 2026. We'll start by covering the basics of how TFMs like TabPFN (the tabular foundation model by Prior Labs) operates, and then dive in to some hands on examples of it in action.

Tuana Celik, Prior Labs
